statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and both of the segments is equal to the square on the whole.
heath_proof: For let the straight line AB be cut at random at the point C; I say that the rectangle contained by AB, BC together with the rectangle contained by BA, AC is equal to the square on AB. For let the square ADEB be described on AB [I. 46], and let CF be drawn through C parallel to either AD or BE. [I. 31]  Then AE is equal to AF, CE. Now AE is the square on AB; AF is the rectangle contained by BA, AC, for it is contained by DA, AC, and AD is equal to AB; and CE is the rectangle AB, BC, for BE is equal to AB. Therefore the rectangle BA, AC together with the rectangle AB, BC is equal to the square on AB.
ai_proof_text:
2.2
**Statement:** If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and both of the segments is equal to the square on the whole.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line AB be cut at random at the point C. It is required to prove that the rectangle contained by AB, AC together with the rectangle contained by AB, BC is equal to the square on AB.

**Step 2.** On AB describe the square ADEB [1.46], with the vertex D adjoining A and the vertex E adjoining B. By the construction of 1.46, the side DE is drawn parallel to AB and the side BE parallel to AD.

**Step 3.** Through C draw CF parallel to AD [1.31], and let it meet DE at F. The straight line CF divides the square AE into the two quadrilaterals AF (that is, ACFD) and CE (that is, CBEF); thus the square AE is made up of the figures AF and CE.

**Step 4.** AF is a parallelogram, for AD is parallel to CF by construction, and AC, DF are parts of the parallel sides AB, DE of the square. Its angles at A and D are angles of the square ADEB and are therefore right [D1.22]; hence its opposite angles at F and at C are also right [1.34], so that AF is a rectangular parallelogram. By D2.1 it is the rectangle contained by DA, AC; and since DA is equal to AB, being sides of the square [D1.22], AF is the rectangle contained by AB, AC.

**Step 5.** In the same way CE is a parallelogram, for CF is parallel to BE by construction, and CB, FE are parts of the parallel sides AB, DE. Its angles at B and E are angles of the square and are right [D1.22]; hence its opposite angles at F and at C are right [1.34], and CE is a rectangular parallelogram. By D2.1 it is the rectangle contained by BE, BC; and since BE is equal to AB [D1.22], CE is the rectangle contained by AB, BC.

**Step 6.** AE is the square on AB, by the construction of Step 2.

**Step 7.** Therefore, since the square AE is made up of AF and CE, the square on AB is equal to the rectangle contained by AB, AC together with the rectangle contained by AB, BC. That is, if a straight line AB is cut at random at C, the rectangles contained by the whole AB and each of the segments AC, CB together equal the square on AB. Q.E.D.

Path note: the result could also be derived from Proposition 2.1 by taking the uncut line equal to AB, but that route needs an extra lemma identifying the rectangle contained by two lines equal to AB with the square on AB; the direct division of the square is chosen because the statement itself concerns the square on AB, which this construction exhibits and divides.
